newsitem.title: CROATIA: SOCCER-ZAGREB STORM PAST PARTIZAN IN EUROPEAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAGREB STORM PAST PARTIZAN IN EUROPEAN CUP.

text.p: Croatia Zagreb thrashed their former Yugoslav arch-rivals Partizan Belgrade 5-0 in the second leg of a European Cup qualifier on Wednesday to clinch a preliminary round encounter with England's Newcastle.
The Croatian champions, formerly Dinamo Zagreb, scored four goals in a first half blitz to easily wipe out the 1-0 deficit from the first leg in Belgrade.
Croatia will now meet Newcastle over two legs in August for a place in the Champions' League.

A 35,000 capacity crowd at the Maksimir stadium, the biggest seen in Zagreb since the break up of the Yugoslav league in 1991, chanted "Vukovar", "Vukovar", the name of the Croatian town levelled by the Serb-dominated Yugoslav army in 1991.
But despite fears of violence a heavy police presence ensured the high-risk clash passed without incident.

Fans celebrated the victory, the first in an official competition over a Serbian soccer club since the 1991-95 war, by honking sirens, waving flags and jumping into a fountain at Zagreb's main square.
Zagreb dominated throughout, allowing Partizan only one chance -- a second-half penalty saved by goalkeeper Drazen Ladic.
Silvio Maric, who squandered several chances in the first leg, opened the scoring in the 13th minute with a sharp shot from close range.
Igor Cvitanovic headed home a cross from the left three minutes later and Mark Viduka fired in a stinging shot from the edge of the area in the 24th.
Croatian international Robert Prosinecki, recently bought from Spain's Seville, and Bosnian Edin Mujcin dominated the midfield, keeping their strikers well supplied.
Maric scored his second from close range just before the break to ensure a comfortable second half for the hosts.
The high point of a quiet second half came in the 69th minute when Cvitanovic hammered home a volley from the edge of the area.
Partizan's penalty followed six minutes later but Dejan Vukicevic's spot kick was saved by Ladic who also blocked a second attempt from the rebound.

Croatia - 1-Drazen Ladic, 3-Damir Krznar, 4-Silvio Maric (18-Vladimir Petrovic 68), 5-Goran Juric, 8-Robert Prosinecki, 9-Mark Viduka (20-Stjepan Tomas 76), 13-Dario Simic, 15-Danijel Saric, 21-Igor Cvitanovic, 24-Krunoslav Jurcic, Edin Mujcin (14-Zoran Brlenic 72)
